blockers.quote: you double-text the crush, then start a fight in the group chat expecting proof that people care, and coins pour in from anger.
blockers.why: story #5: Double-texting and starting the fight are joined by “then”; the first action causes no turn.
blockers.fix: You double-text the crush expecting a coin. Nothing lands. Therefore you provoke the group chat; coins arrive, but every one is angry.

blockers.quote: you double-text the crush, then start a fight in the group chat expecting proof that people care, and coins pour in from anger.
blockers.why: story #6: The double-text is a use of the power, but its result is not stated.
blockers.fix: You double-text the crush expecting a coin. Nothing lands. Therefore you provoke the group chat expecting care; the coins arrive tagged with anger.

suggestions.quote: Every waking thought about you pays one coin, kind or cruel, and the app names who had it.
suggestions.fix: Ground the payment promise when it arises: “Every waking thought pays one coin into your account; ten coins buy today’s chai.”

suggestions.quote: Night: coins dropping one by one at 2 a.m., every one from mom, a skyline of her bar over everyone else's
suggestions.fix: Answer why Mom is so high inside this beat: alternate each drop with Mom packing food, checking the metro time, and hovering over the call button.

suggestions.quote: match cuts carry the same phone-checking pose through graduation, work and old age
suggestions.fix: Make each jump worsen rather than repeat: at graduation you miss Asha waving; at work you ignore her call; in old age the same chair beside you is empty.

keep.quote: Coins are care. At least now you can count it
Asha's row stopped the week yours did.
